newsitem.title: INDIA: India stocks close down, ITC takes a beating.
newsitem.headline: India stocks close down, ITC takes a beating.

text.p: Indian blue chips ended with small losses on Wednesday, with market focus on shares of tobacco conglomerate ITC which fell nearly five percent after the firm announced lower-than-expected 1996/97 profits, traders said.
"Operators got out of their positions on disappointment over the ITC results," said Manish Nathwani, dealer at Bombay brokers Samir Doshi.

ITC, 31.7 percent of which is owned by Britain's tobacco and financial group B.A.T Industries Plc, on Tuesday posted a net profit of 3.42 billion rupees ($95.6 million) against 2.61 billion in 1995/96.
The market had been expecting a profit of up to 4.0 billion rupees, traders said.
"The stock has had a good run-up ahead of the results. So, what we are seeing now is a small correction," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Kotak Securities, the Indian associate of Goldman Sachs.
ITC shares have rocketed about 29 percent since March, as foreign funds and speculators bid the stock ahead of results.
Analysts said ITC's 1996/97 performance was mostly in line with expectations, with a rise in cigarette volumes driving growth.
The tobacco giant is expected to report strong growth in 1997/98 (April-March) on the back of increased sales volumes after a good 1996/97, analysts said.
"Earnings growth will be volume driven, while price hikes will cover increased excise and other costs," said Rajesh Mayani, ITC analyst at HSBC Batlivala & Karani Securities.
"We expect ITC to record a 25 percent earnings growth in 1997/98. This will primarily be achieved from its core cigarette business."
